12016 / what is the difference between tartate and succinate

Evidence

passage 1:9. Get help from a doctor now ›. Medication duration: Succinate (toprol) is the long acting form of metoprolol where as tartrate (lopressor) is the shorter acting form. Toprol can be taken once a day and Lopressor is usually taken at least twice a day....Read more.Great you're all set!. Get help from a doctor now ›. Medication duration: Succinate (toprol) is the long acting form of metoprolol where as tartrate (lopressor) is the shorter acting form. Toprol can be taken once a day and Lopressor is usually taken at least twice a day. passage 2:Tartrate vs Succinate. The key difference between tartrate and succinate is that succinate is derived from the succinic acid and tartrate is derived from the tartaric acid. These two chemical substances are widely used in the beverage industry and drug manufacturing.Succinic acid is ethan-1,2-dicarboxylic acid. Succinate form of metoprolol is an extended release drug and it plays its role in the circulatory system for 24 hours. However, the tartrate form of metoprolol does not appear in the blood stream for 24 hours because metoprolol tartrate is an immediate-release drug. passage 3:Release time. The primary difference between metoprolol succinate and metoprolol tartrate is the length of time that the drugs stay in your bloodstream. Metoprolol succinate will stay in a person's bloodstream for 24 complete hours. This means that the medication is a once per day pill.Metoprolol tartrate, on the other hand, will not stay in the bloodstream as long and thus needs to be taken at regular intervals.etoprolol succinate has a greater dehydrating effect. Thus, the side effects constipation and dry mouth are primarily associated with this version of the medication. Conversely, metoprolol tartrate may cause diarrhea. It also has the potential to cause sleep issues such as insomnia or unusual dreams.

Human annotation

Based on the provided passages, the main differences between tartrate and succinate are: 1. Duration of action: Succinate (Toprol) is a long-acting form of metoprolol, while tartrate (Lopressor) is a shorter-acting form. 2. Release time: Succinate stays in the bloodstream for 24 hours, while tartrate does not last as long and needs to be taken at regular intervals. 3. Side effects: Succinate has a greater dehydrating effect, leading to constipation and dry mouth, while tartrate may cause diarrhea and sleep issues like insomnia or unusual dreams. Therefore, the main difference between tartrate and succinate is the duration of action and the side effects they produce.

12763 / what is the treatment when asset is discarded as per income tax act

Evidence

passage 1:For the purposes of Income Tax Act, a previous year is a distinct unit. In case an asset is discarded by the business but not sold, section 43(6) permits the scrap value of the asset to be reduced from the block in the previous year in which such asset is discarded.nder the block concept, all the assets falling within the same class and subject to same rate of depreciation are clubbed together and considered as single asset. Any alterations to the value of the block have to be strictly in accordance with the provisions of Chapter IV D of Income Tax Act, 1961. passage 2:Illustration 4 Note: The purpose of this illustration is to assist in clarifying the meaning of the explanation toparagraph 13 of theStandard. Facts: 1. The income before depreciation and tax of an enterprise for 15 years is Rs. 1000 lakhs per year, both as per the booksof account and for income-tax purposes.2. The enterprise is subject to 100 percent tax-holiday for the first 10 years under section 80-IA.llustration 4 Note: The purpose of this illustration is to assist in clarifying the meaning of the explanation toparagraph 13 of theStandard. Facts: 1. The income before depreciation and tax of an enterprise for 15 years is Rs. 1000 lakhs per year, both as per the booksof account and for income-tax purposes. passage 3:Pavan Jain S. Depreciation – a non cash expenditure allowed under Income Tax Act, 1961 following block concept. Under the block concept, all the assets falling within the same class and subject to same rate of depreciation are clubbed together and considered as single asset.he assessee is entitled to claim depreciation on the residual value of such discarded asset [ie., Opening WDV of such asset less scrap value] even though such discarded asset is not used for the purposes of business or profession in such year and subsequent years.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, when an asset is discarded but not sold, the scrap value of the asset can be reduced from the block in the previous year in which the asset is discarded. The block concept is followed, where assets of the same class and subject to the same rate of depreciation are grouped together and considered as a single asset. The assessee is entitled to claim depreciation on the residual value of the discarded asset, even if it is not used for business or profession in that year and subsequent years.

13375 / how to peel potatoes fast

Evidence

passage 1:Place washed whole, unpeeled potatoes into a pot and cover with cold water. The “shocking” process of going from the hot boiling water to the cold ice water helps release the skin from the flesh and makes the potato quite easy to peel. passage 2:True the skin comes off fairly easy but it takes so freakin long! Especially if you are peeling a crap load of potatoes. Here is the easiest way (or at least the easiest way I’ve discovered) to peel a cooked potato. Step 1.) Bring a pot of water to a boil. Step 2.) With a knife, score your potatoes all the way around the center. Step 3.) Place your potatoes in the pot and boil for about 15 minutes or so. Step 4.) Prepare a bowl of ice water and place your potatoes in the water. Step 5.) Swish it around for a few seconds just enough so that it’s cool enough to handle. Step 6.) Remove your potatoe from the water and remove the skin. passage 3:You will need. Step 1 Cut the potato skin Make a cut all around the potato, lengthwise. Try to slice only the skin, not the actual potato. Step 2 Boil it Put the potato in a pot of boiling water. Step 3 Cool it off Plunge the potato in ice water for 10 seconds. The surface of the potato will shrink, while the center remains hot. Step 4 Remove the skin Rub the potato with both hands and watch the skin fall right off.

Step 1: Open Settings app. To do so, open Start menu and then click Settings icon. Step 3: In the left-pane, click Default apps. Step 4: Now, on the right-side, scroll down the page to see Web browser section. Step 5: Click on the Edge browser entry (or any browser other than Chrome) to reveal Choose an app, and then click Google Chrome to set it as default browser. passage 3:To set Mozilla Firefox as your default Windows browser, take the following steps. 1 Open your Firefox browser. 2 Click on the Firefox menu button, represented by three horizontal lines and located in the upper right hand corner of the browser window. 3 When the pop-out menu appears, select Options.

Evidence

passage 1:The physiological benefits of hugging. Hugs make you feel good for a reason and it's not just the loving embrace that gives us that warm feeling in our hearts. It's much more. It affects the entire body to such an extent that many scientists claim it is equivalent to the effect of many different drugs operating on the body simultaneously. passage 2:Empathy and Listening Skills. and. Psychological Hugs. The use of empathy and listening skills--empathic listening--sometimes leads to good relationships, emotional intimacy, and happy marriages. Their use may also lead to a conversation partner feeling like she or he is receiving a hug--a psychological hug.. passage 3:In a study on fears and self-esteem, research published in the journal Psychological Science revealed that hugs and touch significantly reduce worry of mortality. The studies found that hugging -- even if it was just an inanimate object like a teddy bear -- helps soothe individuals' existential fears.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, here are the psychological effects of hugging: 1. Reduces stress and anxiety: Hugging releases oxytocin, which can lower blood pressure and heart rate, and reduce stress and anxiety (Passage 1). 2. Improves mood and well-being: Hugs can boost feelings of happiness and social connection, leading to improved overall mood and well-being (Passage 1). 3. Enhances empathy and listening skills: Physical touch, such as hugging, can increase empathy and improve listening skills, leading to better relationships and emotional intimacy (Passage 2). 4. Soothes existential fears: Hugging can help alleviate fears of mortality and provide a sense of comfort and security (Passage 3). Therefore, hugging has several positive psychological effects, including reducing stress and anxiety, improving mood and well-being, enhancing empathy and listening skills, and soothing existential fears.

13129 / how to soften sugar

Evidence

passage 1:3-Place brown sugar in a plastic container with a small piece of plastic wrap or foil over the sugar. Put a damp paper towel or napkin on top of the plastic/foil. Cover tightly. Remove damp paper towel in a couple of days. passage 2:A. Granulated sugar will harden when exposed to any type of moisture. Here is an easy way to make hardened granulated sugar soft again -- Preheat oven to lowest temperature, 150-200 degrees. Remove sugar from the package and put in an ovenproof container that will hold the sugar. Place in the warm oven for approximately 15 minutes. Tap sugar with a spoon. If it starts to fall apart, turn oven off and leave sugar in the oven for an hour or two to completely dry out. Always store granulated sugar in an airtight container. Store confectioners sugar in a cool, dry location (not the refrigerator). When it gets moist, it develops lumps. passage 3:How to keep it soft. The most efficient way to keep brown sugar soft is to keep it sealed in an airtight container. The trick is to limit the amount of air exposure as much as possible. Pack the sugar into the smallest container possible so that there is hardly any air space between the sugar and the lid.

Human annotation

Passage 1 suggests placing brown sugar in a plastic container with a small piece of plastic wrap or foil over it, then covering it tightly with a damp paper towel or napkin. Passage 2 provides a method for softening granulated sugar by preheating the oven to the lowest temperature, placing the sugar in an ovenproof container, and warming it for approximately 15 minutes. If the sugar starts to fall apart, it should be left in the warm oven for an hour or two to completely dry out. Passage 3 advises keeping brown sugar soft by storing it in an airtight container with limited air exposure.

Evidence

passage 1:Place washed whole, unpeeled potatoes into a pot and cover with cold water. Especially if you are peeling a crap load of potatoes. Here is the easiest way (or at least the easiest way I’ve discovered) to peel a cooked potato. Step 1.) Bring a pot of water to a boil. Step 2.) With a knife, score your potatoes all the way around the center. Step 3.) Place your potatoes in the pot and boil for about 15 minutes or so. Step 4.) Prepare a bowl of ice water and place your potatoes in the water. Step 5.) Swish it around for a few seconds just enough so that it’s cool enough to handle. Step 6.) Remove your potatoe from the water and remove the skin. passage 3:You will need. Step 1 Cut the potato skin Make a cut all around the potato, lengthwise. Try to slice only the skin, not the actual potato. Step 2 Boil it Put the potato in a pot of boiling water. Step 3 Cool it off Plunge the potato in ice water for 10 seconds. The surface of the potato will shrink, while the center remains hot. Step 4 Remove the skin Rub the potato with both hands and watch the skin fall right off.

17054 / inventory costing weighted average

Evidence

passage 1:Instead, the weighted average method of costing inventory assigns an average cost to each piece of inventory when it is sold. When unit of inventory is sold, the weighted average method of costing inventory takes the average cost of all inventories currently available.This average price is then assigned to the item sold. Since inventory prices fluctuate, the weighted average cost will also change.Think about it this way.hen unit of inventory is sold, the weighted average method of costing inventory takes the average cost of all inventories currently available. This average price is then assigned to the item sold. Since inventory prices fluctuate, the weighted average cost will also change. Think about it this way. passage 2:When using the weighted average method, divide the cost of goods available for sale by the number of units available for sale, which yields the weighted-average cost per unit. In this calculation, the cost of goods available for sale is the sum of beginning inventory and net purchases.You then use this weighted-average figure to assign a cost to both ending inventory and the cost of goods sold.The net result of using weighted average costing is that the recorded amount of inventory on hand represents a value somewhere between the oldest and newest units purchased into stock.eighted average costing is commonly used in situations where: 1 Inventory items are so intermingled that it is impossible to assign a specific cost to an individual unit. 2 The accounting system is not sufficiently sophisticated to track FIFO or LIFO inventory layers. passage 3:The weighted average method is an inventory costing method that assigns average costs to each piece of inventory when it is sold during the year.Retailers and other businesses that keep and sell inventory must keep track of the cost of inventory on hand as well as the cost of inventory that was sold.hen unit of inventory is sold, the weighted average method of costing inventory takes the average cost of all inventories currently available. This average price is then assigned to the item sold. Since inventory prices fluctuate, the weighted average cost will also change. Think about it this way.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, it can be understood that the Weighted Average Costing (WAC) method is used to determine the average cost of inventory when a unit is sold. This method takes the average cost of all inventories currently available and uses it to calculate the weighted average cost per unit. WAC is commonly used when inventory items are intermingled and it's difficult to assign a specific cost to an individual unit, or when the accounting system is not sophisticated enough to track FIFO or LIFO inventory layers.

13530 / difference between feha and ada

Evidence

passage 1:One difference between the FEHA (the Fair Employment and Housing Act) and the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) is that the ADA applies to all employers in the private sector that have four to fifteen employees, whereas the FEHA affects more employees, and it doesn’t distinguish between private and public employers like the ADA does. passage 2:Class Description: This class is designed specifically for supervisors and managers to learn the basic provisions of the California's Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and understand their responsibilities during the reasonable accommodation process. passage 3:Probably one of the most important differences between the ADA and FEHA is that with FEHA, a disability is required. Under the ADA, to qualify for disability, a physical or mental impairment substantially limits a major life activity, but the FEHA requires only that a mental and physical disability limit a major life activity; not a substantial limit, but a limit.

Human annotation

The FEHA (Fair Employment and Housing Act) and the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) have several differences. The ADA applies to all employers in the private sector that have four to fifteen employees, while the FEHA affects more employees and does not distinguish between private and public employers. Another important difference is the requirement of disability. The ADA requires a physical or mental impairment to substantially limit a major life activity, while the FEHA only requires that a mental and physical disability limit a major life activity, without the need for it to be a substantial limit.

Mix paint that’s two shades darker than your basecoat with an equal amount of glaze.Once your basecoat dries, drip a crumpled rag or plastic bag in the glaze mixture.ive new wood a vintage look with paint. You don’t have to wait decades for your wood pieces to acquire a vintage look. Instead, duplicate the age-worn finishes you see in antique stores with decorative painting techniques. You can give your wooden furniture, accessories and cabinetry a vintage patina in little time.

Human annotation

To give wood an antique effect using normal paint, start by painting the wood piece with a basecoat of flat or satin paint. Satin paint is easier to work with, but flat paint gives an older look. Once the basecoat dries, mix paint that's two shades darker than your basecoat with an equal amount of glaze. Dab a crumpled rag or plastic bag in the glaze mixture and apply it to the wood. You can also layer stain for a cool, antique effect. Apply the stain, distress the wood, then apply another layer of stain. Another technique involves applying a layer of molding paste which dries white, then mixing in a rust or dull color such as yellow ochre or paynes grey, spreading it over the wood, and letting it dry.

To give wood an antique effect using normal paint, start by painting the wood piece with a basecoat of flat or satin paint. Satin paint is easier to work with, but flat paint gives an older look. Once the basecoat dries, mix paint that's two shades darker than your basecoat with an equal amount of glaze. Dab a crumpled rag or plastic bag in the glaze mixture and apply it to the wood. You can also layer stain for a cool, antique effect. Apply the stain, distress the wood, then apply another layer of stain. Another technique involves applying a layer of molding paste which dries white, then mixing in a rust or dull color such as yellow ochre or paynes grey, spreading it over the wood, and letting it dry.

16936 / what happens when you breath in and out

Evidence

passage 1:Breathing Out (Exhalation) When you breathe out, or exhale, your diaphragm relaxes and moves upward into the chest cavity. The intercostal muscles between the ribs also relax to reduce the space in the chest cavity. As the space in the chest cavity gets smaller, air rich in carbon dioxide is forced out of your lungs and windpipe, and then out of your nose or mouth. Breathing out requires no effort from your body unless you have a lung disease or are doing physical activity. passage 2:When you inhale: 1 the intercostal muscles contract, expanding the ribcage. 2 the diaphragm contracts, pulling downwards to increase the volume of the chest. 3 pressure inside the chest is lowered and air is sucked into the lungs. passage 3:When you breath, the outside air pushes into your windpipe (trachea) into your lungs. When there is a hole in the chest wall, the outside air can come in through that hole. The air gathers around the lung and collapses it. With a large amount of air around the outside of the lung, it can't expand.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, here is what happens when you breathe in and out: When you breathe in (inhalation): * The intercostal muscles contract, causing the ribcage to expand. * The diaphragm contracts, pulling downwards to increase the volume of the chest. * Pressure inside the chest is lowered, allowing air to be sucked into the lungs. When you breathe out (exhalation): * The diaphragm relaxes and moves upward into the chest cavity. * The intercostal muscles relax, reducing the space in the chest cavity. * Air rich in carbon dioxide is forced out of the lungs and windpipe, and then out of the nose or mouth. So, in summary, when you breathe in, the diaphragm and intercostal muscles contract to bring air into the lungs, and when you breathe out, the diaphragm and intercostal muscles relax to force air out of the lungs.

DMSO, or dimethyl sulfoxide, is used in a variety of ways both industrially and medically. Industrially, it is used as an antifreeze and a solvent for numerous chemicals. Medically, DMSO is applied to the skin as an anti-inflammatory and general pain reliever, most commonly for muscles and joints. It is also used to promote healing for minor cuts, burns, soft tissue damage, local tissue death, and skin ulcers. DMSO has the unique ability to penetrate skin and tissue, allowing it to enter the bloodstream.

Evidence

passage 1:If it is the heavy plastic kind, you can make a casing in the side seams by stitching the outer edge of the gusset and that back side seam. Then, slide that boning right down into that casing. In this case that means 2″. You are basically going to add 2 total inches to the left side of your dress and 2 total inches to the right side. Measure out to the left of that main dot one inch and make a second dot. passage 2:Make a zipper sandwich. Place 1 piece of lining fabric face up, then the zipper and then the outer fabric right side facing down. Line up the three edges. With a zipper foot sew across the top between the edge of your zipper sandwich and the zipper teeth (closer to the zipper feet).When finished and you pull fabric back it will look like this. Repeat this for the other side(edge) of the zipper. Oops the fabric should go all the way to the end of the zipper.ake a zipper sandwich. Place 1 piece of lining fabric face up, then the zipper and then the outer fabric right side facing down. Line up the three edges. Make a few stitches near the top stop of the zipper. Pin the zipper gusset to the zipper (1/4″ away from the center) with right side facing each other. Change the presser foot to zipper foot, sew a line near to the seam line to secure the position.Place the zipper gusset lining on top of them with right side facing down. Stitch on the seam line.Flip the lining to the bottom of main zipper gusset, top stitch near the seam line. Repeat sewing another side of the zipper gusset.The width of the zipper in between the gusset should measure 1/2″. Change the presser foot back to normal foot, stitch on the seam allowance around the zipper gusset so that the main and lining fabric attach together nicely.lip lightly on the piping seam allowance at the curve. Human annotation

Sure! Here's how to sew a zipper gusset based on the provided passages: To sew a zipper gusset, follow these steps: 1. Make a zipper sandwich by placing a piece of lining fabric face up, then the zipper, and finally the outer fabric right side facing down. Line up the three edges and sew across the top using a zipper foot. Repeat this process for the other side of the zipper. (Passage 2) 2. Trace the pattern onto the remaining fabric and cut it. Make a few stitches near the top stop of the zipper. Pin the zipper gusset to the zipper with right sides facing each other, and sew a line near the seam line to secure its position. (Passage 3) 3. Place the zipper gusset lining on top of the main zipper gusset with right sides facing down, and stitch along the seam line. Flip the lining to the bottom of the main zipper gusset, and topstitch near the seam line. Repeat the process for the other side of the zipper gusset. The width of the zipper between the gusset should measure 1/2". (Passage 3) That's it! Based on the provided passages, there is no additional information needed to answer the question.

13071 / what is psa levels mean

Evidence

passage 1:Prostate-specific antigen, or PSA, is a protein produced by cells of the prostate gland. The PSA test measures the level of PSA in a man’s blood.For this test, a blood sample is sent to a laboratory for analysis. The results are usually reported as nanograms of PSA per milliliter (ng/mL) of blood.The blood level of PSA is often elevated in men with prostate cancer, and the PSA test was originally approved by the FDA in 1986 to monitor the progression of prostate cancer in men who had already been diagnosed with the disease.he PSA test measures the level of PSA in a man’s blood. For this test, a blood sample is sent to a laboratory for analysis. The results are usually reported as nanograms of PSA per milliliter (ng/mL) of blood. passage 2:A. A. A. Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is a substance produced by the prostate gland. Elevated PSA levels may indicate prostate cancer, a noncancerous condition such as prostatitis, or an enlarged prostate.. A. A. Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is a substance produced by the prostate gland. Elevated PSA levels may indicate prostate cancer, a noncancerous condition such as prostatitis, or an enlarged prostate. passage 3:1 Total PSA levels between 4.0 ng/ml and 10.0 ng/ml may indicate prostate cancer (about a 25% chance, according to the ACS), benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH) , or inflammation of the prostate. 2 These conditions are more common in the elderly, as is a general increase in PSA levels.f the DRE is normal but the PSA is moderately elevated, a free PSA test may be used to look at the ratio of free to total PSA. This can help to distinguish between prostate cancer and other non-cancer causes of elevated PSA.

Human annotation

Based on the provided passages, PSA (Prostate-Specific Antigen) levels refer to the measure of the amount of PSA proteins present in a man's blood. The PSA test is used to detect and monitor prostate cancer, as well as non-cancerous conditions such as prostatitis and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). The test involves taking a blood sample to be analyzed in a laboratory, and the results are typically reported as ng/mL (nanograms per milliliter) of blood. From the passages, we can infer the following meanings of PSA levels: * Elevated PSA levels may indicate prostate cancer, prostatitis, or an enlarged prostate. (Passage 2) * Total PSA levels between 4.0 ng/ml and 10.0 ng/ml may indicate prostate cancer, BPH, or inflammation of the prostate, with a higher likelihood in the elderly. (Passage 3) * Free PSA test can help to distinguish between prostate cancer and other non-cancer causes of elevated PSA levels. (Passage 3) Therefore, based on the provided passages, the answer to the question "What does PSA levels mean?" is: PSA levels refer to the amount of PSA proteins present in a man's blood, and elevated levels may indicate prostate cancer, prostatitis, or an enlarged prostate.

Human annotation

Based on the provided passages, here are some steps to achieve an antique effect on wood using normal paint: 1. Apply a basecoat of flat or satin paint to the wood surface ( passage 3). Satin paint is easier to work with, but flat paint will give a more aged look. 2. Mix paint that is two shades darker than the basecoat with an equal amount of glaze ( passage 3). Once the basecoat is dry, drizzle a crumpled rag or plastic bag in the glaze mixture to achieve an aged appearance. 3. Layer stain on top of the paint to create a cool effect ( passage 1). This technique involves applying multiple layers of stain and allowing them to dry between coats. 4. Use a palette knife to spread a mixture of molding paste and a rust or dull color on a canvas, letting it dry before adding additional layers ( passage 2). This can help create an embossed design with an antique finish. 5. Apply a thin layer of burnt sienna or a similar color to give the wood a vintage look ( passage 3). Dabbing the paint with a paper towel or cloth can help remove excess paint and achieve a more subtle, aged appearance. Overall, the key to achieving an antique effect on wood using normal paint is to layer different materials and colors to create a weathered and worn appearance.

13292 / what causes necrotizing fasciitis

Evidence

passage 1:Necrotizing Fasciitis Causes. Necrotizing fasciitis is caused by bacteria in the vast majority of cases, though fungi can also rarely lead to this condition as well.Many cases of necrotizing fasciitis are caused by group A beta-hemolytic streptococci (Streptococcus pyogenes), either individually or along with other bacterial pathogens.Group A streptococcus is the same bacteria responsible for strep throat , impetigo (skin infection), and rheumatic fever.n many cases of necrotizing fasciitis, there is a history of prior trauma, such as a cut, scrape, insect bite, burn, or needle puncture wound. These lesions may initially appear trivial or minor. Surgical incision sites and various surgical procedures may also serve as a source of infection. passage 2:Causes of Necrotizing Fasciitis. Necrotizing fasciitis is commonly caused by group A Streptococcus (GAS) bacteria. That's the same type of bacteria that causes strep throat.However, several types of bacteria, such as staphylococcus and others, have also been associated with the disease.Necrotizing fasciitis occurs when such bacteria infect the superficial fascia, a layer of connective tissue below the skin.owever, several types of bacteria, such as staphylococcus and others, have also been associated with the disease. Necrotizing fasciitis occurs when such bacteria infect the superficial fascia, a layer of connective tissue below the skin. passage 3:Necrotizing fasciitis is caused by several kinds of bacteria. Some of these bacteria also cause infections such as strep throat and impetigo. Usually the infections caused by these bacteria are mild.But in rare cases they can cause a more dangerous infection.ecrotizing fasciitis is an infection caused by bacteria. It can destroy skin, fat, and the tissue covering the muscles within a very short time. The disease sometimes is called flesh-eating bacteria. When it occurs on the genitals, it is called Fournier gangrene. Necrotizing fasciitis is very rare but serious.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, necrotizing fasciitis is primarily caused by bacteria, specifically group A beta-hemolytic streptococci (Streptococcus pyogenes). However, other bacterial pathogens such as staphylococcus and others have also been associated with the disease. Infections in the superficial fascia, a layer of connective tissue below the skin, are responsible for causing the condition. Trauma, cuts, scrapes, insect bites, burns, needle puncture wounds, and even surgical incisions and procedures may serve as sources of infection.

12432 / symptoms and causes of ibs

Evidence

passage 1:The cause of irritable bowel syndrome is currently unknown. It is thought to result from a combination of abnormal gastrointestinal (GI) tract movements, increased awareness of bodily functions, and a disruption in the communication between the brain and the GI tract. IBS-D is irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea. passage 2:The exact cause of irritable bowel syndrome is unknown. It is believed to be due to a number of factors, including alteration in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract motility, abnormal nervous system signals, increased sensitivity to pain, and food intolerances. The following are risk factors thought to cause IBS: 1 Abnormal movements of the colon and small intestines (too fast or slow, or too strong) 2 Hypersensitivity to pain from a full bowel or gas. 3 Food sensitivities, possibly caused by poor absorption of sugars or acids in food. passage 3:People with IBS have symptoms that can include: 1 Diarrhea (often described as violent episodes of diarrhea) 2 Constipation. 3 Constipation alternating with diarrhea. Belly pains or cramps, usually in the lower half of the belly, that get worse after meals and feel better after a bowel 1 movement. A lot of gas or bloating.

Human annotation

The cause of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is unknown. However, it is believed to be a result of abnormal gastrointestinal (GI) tract movements, increased awareness of bodily functions, disruption in communication between the brain and the GI tract, abnormal nervous system signals, increased sensitivity to pain, and food intolerances. Risk factors may include abnormal movements of the colon and small intestines (either too fast or slow, or too strong), hypersensitivity to pain from a full bowel or gas, and food sensitivities possibly caused by poor absorption of sugars or acids in food. Symptoms of IBS can include diarrhea, constipation, or alternating between the two, belly pains or cramps that worsen after meals and feel better after a bowel movement, as well as a lot of gas or bloating.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, we can understand that there are two types of amino acids - essential and non-essential. Essential amino acids are those that cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through our diet. On the other hand, non-essential amino acids can be synthesized by the body, either from essential amino acids or from breaking down protein products. Thus, it is not necessary to obtain these amino acids from our diet. Therefore, the main difference between essential and non-essential amino acids is that the former must be obtained from food, while the latter can be made by the body.

Human annotation

Based on the provided passages, here is how to make panko crumbs: Passage 1 states to push torn pieces of bread through the shredding disk of a food processor to make coarse crumbs. Then, spread the crumbs on a baking sheet and bake in a preheated oven until they are dry but not toasted, about 6 to 8 minutes. Passage 2 provides similar instructions, stating to push chunks of white bread through the shredding disk of a food processor to make coarse crumbs. Then, spread the crumbs on a baking sheet and bake at 300°F until the crumbs are dry but not toasted, about 6 to 8 minutes. Passage 3 provides additional information, suggesting to preheat the oven to 300°F before making the crumbs. The passage also recommends using a blender carafe to pulse the bread until coarse crumbs form, and then spreading the crumbs evenly on two half-sheet pans and baking until they just begin to brown and are crisp, about 5 minutes. After cooling the crumbs on the pans for 15 to 20 minutes, transfer them to an airtight container and store them at room temperature for up to 2 weeks. Therefore, to make panko crumbs based on the provided passages, you can use a food processor or blender to shred or pulse bread into coarse crumbs, and then bake them in a preheated oven until they are dry but not toasted.

Human annotation

Based on the provided passages, here are the steps to factory reset an HTC One VX: 1. Slide the Notifications panel open. 2. Tap on Storage. 3. Tap on Factory data reset. 4. Tap on Reset phone. 5. Tap on Erase everything. Alternatively, you can also perform a factory reset by following these steps: 1. Hold down the Power button until the device shuts down. 2. Press and hold the Volume Down and Power buttons together for a few seconds until the bootloader mode appears. 3. Use the Volume down button to scroll to "Recovery Mode" and press the Power button to select. 4. From the recovery menu, select "Wipe Data/Factory Reset" and press the Power button to confirm. 5. Wait for the process to complete. 6. Once the reset is done, select "Reboot System" from the recovery menu and press the Power button to restart the device. Please note that performing a factory reset will erase all data on the device, so make sure to back up any important data before doing so.

Based on the given passages, it appears that salary exchange pension contributions refer to a arrangement where an employee agrees to give up part of their salary or bonus in exchange for a pension payment paid by their employer. This can allow both employers and employees to save money, as employers pay lower National Insurance Contributions (NICs) as a result of paying their employees a reduced salary. The salary waived under the salary exchange is equal to the value of the regular pension contribution to the relevant pension scheme, and the university pays a corresponding amount into the scheme. Therefore, it seems that salary exchange pension contributions are a way for employees to make pension contributions by sacrificing part of their salary, while also benefiting from lower NICs, and for employers to contribute to their employees' pensions while also saving on NICs.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, here's a step-by-step guide on how to remove plastic from a clothes dryer: 1. Run the dryer on a regular setting for 20 minutes to soften the plastic. 2. Scrape the plastic off with a wooden or plastic spatula or paint scraper, taking care not to damage the dryer's interior. 3. Apply 1 to 2 tsp. nail polish remover to a clean cloth, and rub the plastic to dissolve it. 4. Rub the area with a damp cloth to rinse the nail polish remover. 5. Mix 1 tsp. liquid laundry soap with 1 cup water. Dip a clean cloth in this solution, and rub the area again. 6. Rinse well with a cloth dipped in clean water. If the plastic does not come off with this method, another option is to use a hair dryer or heat gun to heat the plastic until it becomes soft and pliable. Then, attempt to peel it off carefully. However, be aware that this method may not work, and in that case, replacing the drum or the entire dryer may be necessary. It is recommended to call a service technician for this type of repair. Therefore, the answer to the question of how to get plastic out of clothes dryer is: 1. Run the dryer on a regular setting for 20 minutes to soften the plastic. 2. Scrape the plastic off with a wooden or plastic spatula or paint scraper. 3. Apply nail polish remover to dissolve the plastic. 4. Rinse with a damp cloth and soap solution. 5. Use a hair dryer or heat gun to heat the plastic if necessary. If the plastic still does not come off, consider replacing the drum or the entire dryer.

12015 / what is the difference between tartate and succinate

Evidence

passage 1:9. Get help from a doctor now ›. Medication duration: Succinate (toprol) is the long acting form of metoprolol where as tartrate (lopressor) is the shorter acting form. Toprol can be taken once a day and Lopressor is usually taken at least twice a day....Read more.Great you're all set!. Get help from a doctor now ›. Medication duration: Succinate (toprol) is the long acting form of metoprolol where as tartrate (lopressor) is the shorter acting form. Toprol can be taken once a day and Lopressor is usually taken at least twice a day. passage 2:Tartrate vs Succinate. The key difference between tartrate and succinate is that succinate is derived from the succinic acid and tartrate is derived from the tartaric acid. These two chemical substances are widely used in the beverage industry and drug manufacturing.Succinic acid is ethan-1,2-dicarboxylic acid. Succinate form of metoprolol is an extended release drug and it plays its role in the circulatory system for 24 hours. However, the tartrate form of metoprolol does not appear in the blood stream for 24 hours because metoprolol tartrate is an immediate-release drug. passage 3:Release time. The primary difference between metoprolol succinate and metoprolol tartrate is the length of time that the drugs stay in your bloodstream. Metoprolol succinate will stay in a person's bloodstream for 24 complete hours. This means that the medication is a once per day pill.Metoprolol tartrate, on the other hand, will not stay in the bloodstream as long and thus needs to be taken at regular intervals.etoprolol succinate has a greater dehydrating effect. Thus, the side effects constipation and dry mouth are primarily associated with this version of the medication. Conversely, metoprolol tartrate may cause diarrhea. It also has the potential to cause sleep issues such as insomnia or unusual dreams.

Formation: Succinate is derived from succinic acid, while tartrate is derived from tartaric acid. Therefore, the answer to the question is: Difference between tartate and succinate: Succinate is derived from succinic acid, while tartrate is derived from tartaric acid; Succinate stays in the bloodstream for 24 hours, while tartrate does not.

Evidence

passage 1:How does a reverse raffle work? ♦ The reverse raffle is a raffle but backwards. ♦ Your entry ticket has a number on it from 1 to approximately 55. ♦ Tickets are $50 each and a table consists of 20 individuals, which constitutes one complete ticket at $1000. and two $500 prizes (one for the early bird drawing and one for the first ticket pulled). individuals totaling twenty. passage 2:How does the 50-50 draw work? The gross proceeds of 50-50 tickets sold at the event go into a prize pool. 50% of the prize pool will go to the winner of the random draw which occurs towards the end of the event. The remaining 50% will be set aside for a charitable purpose chosen by the sporting club. passage 3:Drinks and dinner are included with your ticket price. ♦ In addition to your ticket entry, you will have the opportunity to participate in cash tip board raffles. not included in the ticket price. have the chance to win $10,000!!

Human annotation

Raffles are games of chance where participants buy tickets for a chance to win a prize. The reverse raffle is a type of raffle where the winner is determined by subtracting their ticket number from the highest number in the game. For example, if the highest number in the game is 55 and your ticket number is 47, then you would win the game. Tickets are usually sold at a fixed price, such as $50 per ticket. The 50-50 draw is another type of raffle that takes place during an event. Participants can buy tickets by roaming staff who use handheld electronic mobile devices to sell them. The gross proceeds of ticket sales are used to create a prize pool. At the end of the event, 50% of the prize pool is randomly awarded to one winner, while the other 50% is set aside for a charitable cause. In some cases, participants may also have the opportunity to participate in cash tip board raffles. These raffles offer a chance to win large sums of money, such as $10,000.

14364 / how to get rid of ticks from dogs

Evidence

passage 1:Be sure to check inside and behind his ears and around his eyes, all favorite tick hiding places. To remove a tick, follow these steps: Use a pair of tweezers to grasp the head of the tick where it attaches to the skin. Wear gloves if you plan to use your fingers to remove the tick.Pull on the tick gently and steadily. If you yank the tick away from your dog too quickly, you’ll leave part of the tick’s mouth behind, which can cause an infection.e sure to check inside and behind his ears and around his eyes, all favorite tick hiding places. To remove a tick, follow these steps: Use a pair of tweezers to grasp the head of the tick where it attaches to the skin. Wear gloves if you plan to use your fingers to remove the tick. passage 2:The best way to prevent ticks from attaching to your dog is by the regular use of tick control products. Your veterinarian can advise you about the best product for your dog and your situation. Your veterinarian is also aware of diseases that are common in your area and can pose a risk to your dog.icks can attach to and feed on humans. The skin where ticks attach to humans can become red and irritated. Ticks that transmit diseases to your dog can also transmit many of the same diseases to people. It is important to realize that people do not get these diseases from their dogs. passage 3:Fleas are the most common cause of skin disease in dogs and cats. When a flea bites, it injects saliva into your pet’s skin. This may trigger an allergic reaction. Signs include intense itching, hair loss (especially just in front of the tail), scabs, and red, irritated skin, which may lead to skin infections.lea and tick shampoos are mainly useful for killing the fleas and ticks that are already on your pet. They don’t work as well to prevent ticks. Make sure you get the right kind. Some products for dogs can kill cats.

Human annotation

To get rid of ticks from dogs, first, check common tick hiding places such as inside and behind the dog's ears and around the eyes. Once you locate a tick, use a pair of tweezers to grasp the tick's head where it attaches to the skin. If you plan to use your fingers, wear gloves. Pull on the tick gently and steadily to avoid leaving part of the tick's mouth behind, which can cause an infection. Regular use of tick control products can also prevent ticks from attaching to your dog. Your veterinarian can advise you about the best product for your dog and your situation. Flea and tick shampoos can kill the ticks that are already on your pet.

13138 / how to change the sleep time on my computer

Evidence

passage 1:Step 1: Click Start Menu to load the Help Center. Step 2: Enter Power Management Settings in the search field. Step 3: Click Change Power Management settings. The Power Options window will then appear. Step 4: On the left side of the window, click Change when the computer sleeps. Step 5: Change the Put the computer to sleep entry with the desired amount of time you will allow the computer to sit idle before it sleeps, or automatically turn off its option to enter into Sleep mode. Windows 7. Step 1: Click Start Menu, select Control Panel. passage 2:For a lot of PCs (especially laptops and tablets), your PC goes to sleep when you close your lid or press the power button. To make your PC sleep: Open power options: For Windows 10, in the search box on the taskbar, type power options and then select Power Options. passage 3:Select the Start button and then select Power > Shut down. For Windows 8.1 / Windows RT 8.1. Move your mouse to the lower left-hand corner of the screen and right-click the Start button or press Windows logo key + X on your keyboard. Tap or click Shut down or sign out and choose Shut down.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, here is how you can change the sleep time on your computer: Passage 1: Step 1: Click Start Menu to load the Help Center. Step 2: Enter Power Management Settings in the search field. Step 3: Click Change Power Management settings. Step 4: On the left side of the window, click Change when the computer sleeps. Step 5: Change the Put the computer to sleep entry with the desired amount of time you will allow the computer to sit idle before it sleeps, or automatically turn off its option to enter into Sleep mode. Passage 2: For a lot of PCs (especially laptops and tablets), your PC goes to sleep when you close your lid or press the power button. Passage 3: Select the Start button and then select Power > Shut down. Therefore, to change the sleep time on your computer, you need to follow these steps: 1. Click Start Menu to load the Help Center. 2. Enter Power Management Settings in the search field. 3. Click Change Power Management settings. 4. On the left side of the window, click Change when the computer sleeps. 5. Change the Put the computer to sleep entry with the desired amount of time you will allow the computer to sit idle before it sleeps, or automatically turn off its option to enter into Sleep mode. Alternatively, you can also use the shortcut keys Windows key + X and select Power Options from the menu to open the Power Options window directly.

Place the zipper gusset pieces on top of the zipper, with the right sides facing each other, and sew a line near the seam line to secure the position. Then, place the zipper gusset lining on top of the zipper gusset, with the right side facing down, and stitch on the seam line. Flip the lining to the bottom of the main zipper gusset and topstitch near the seam line. Repeat the process for the other side of the zipper gusset. The width of the zipper in between the gusset should measure 1/2". Finally, stitch on the seam allowance around the zipper gusset to attach the main and lining fabrics together. 15676 / factors that cause oily skin

Evidence

passage 1:Oily Skin Causes. People with oily skin often wonder what they're doing to cause the problem. They may blame it on the greasy pizza they ate last night, but the truth is they should probably blame their genes.Diet can aggravate acne, but it doesn't cause oily skin [source: WebMD ].Oily skin is hereditary -- you can change your diet or change your lifestyle, but if your mom or dad has oily skin, chances are you will, too.However, if your oily skin comes and goes, it may have less to do with genes and more to do with hormonal shifts in your body.ily Skin Causes. People with oily skin often wonder what they're doing to cause the problem. They may blame it on the greasy pizza they ate last night, but the truth is they should probably blame their genes. passage 2:Oily skin is a term commonly used to identify skin that feels ‘oily’ or appears ‘shiny’, especially the skin of the face. Before investigating the cause of your oily skin, it is important to first identify if this ‘oiliness’ is a natural phenomenon or due to poor hygiene and topical applications.ontrary to popular belief, your diet has a limited effect on the oiliness of the skin. A common myth is that oily foods, especially foods like chocolates and peanut butter, may increase the oil production. Alcohol is often thought to be responsible as well. passage 3:Skin types include normal, oily, dry, and sensitive. Some people also have a combination of skin types in different areas of their skin. Your skin type can change over time. For example, younger people are more likely than older people to have a normal skin type. combination skin type can be dry or normal in some areas and oily in others, such as the T-zone (nose, forehead, and chin). Many people have combination skin, which may benefit from slightly different types of skin care in different areas. Combination skin can produce: 1 Overly dilated pores. 2 Blackheads. 3 Shiny skin.

Human annotation

Based on the provided passages, the factors that contribute to oily skin are: 1. Genetics: Oily skin can be inherited from parents, and individuals with a family history of oily skin are more likely to experience it themselves. 2. Hormonal changes: Hormonal fluctuations in the body can lead to oily skin, especially during puberty, menstruation, pregnancy, and menopause. 3. Poor hygiene and topical applications: Using heavy or oily cosmetic products, not washing the face regularly, and not removing makeup properly can contribute to oily skin. It is important to note that diet does not significantly affect oily skin, and popular beliefs about certain foods increasing oil production are not supported by evidence.

17057 / inventory costing weighted average

Evidence

passage 1:Instead, the weighted average method of costing inventory assigns an average cost to each piece of inventory when it is sold. When unit of inventory is sold, the weighted average method of costing inventory takes the average cost of all inventories currently available.This average price is then assigned to the item sold. Since inventory prices fluctuate, the weighted average cost will also change.Think about it this way.hen unit of inventory is sold, the weighted average method of costing inventory takes the average cost of all inventories currently available. This average price is then assigned to the item sold. Since inventory prices fluctuate, the weighted average cost will also change. Think about it this way. passage 2:When using the weighted average method, divide the cost of goods available for sale by the number of units available for sale, which yields the weighted-average cost per unit. In this calculation, the cost of goods available for sale is the sum of beginning inventory and net purchases.You then use this weighted-average figure to assign a cost to both ending inventory and the cost of goods sold.The net result of using weighted average costing is that the recorded amount of inventory on hand represents a value somewhere between the oldest and newest units purchased into stock.eighted average costing is commonly used in situations where: 1 Inventory items are so intermingled that it is impossible to assign a specific cost to an individual unit. 2 The accounting system is not sufficiently sophisticated to track FIFO or LIFO inventory layers. passage 3:The weighted average method is an inventory costing method that assigns average costs to each piece of inventory when it is sold during the year.Retailers and other businesses that keep and sell inventory must keep track of the cost of inventory on hand as well as the cost of inventory that was sold.hen unit of inventory is sold, the weighted average method of costing inventory takes the average cost of all inventories currently available. This average price is then assigned to the item sold. Since inventory prices fluctuate, the weighted average cost will also change. Think about it this way.

Human annotation

Sure, I can help you with that! Based on the given passages, here's a brief answer to your question: The weighted average method of inventory costing assigns an average cost to each piece of inventory when it is sold. The cost of goods available for sale is divided by the number of units available for sale to calculate the weighted-average cost per unit. This figure is then used to assign a cost to both ending inventory and the cost of goods sold. The weighted average method is commonly used when inventory items are intermingled and cannot be assigned a specific cost, or when the accounting system is not sophisticated enough to track FIFO or LIFO inventory layers.

16774 / similarity and difference between nervous system and endocrine system

Evidence

passage 1:Key Differences. The nervous system is made of neuron cells while the Endocrine System is made of glands. Transmission is performed by the electrochemical pulses in nervous system. On the contrary, the Chemicals known as hormones are responsible for signal transmission in Endocrine System. passage 2:The nervous system is continuous in which the cells are interconnected. In contrast, the organs of the Endocrine System are not physically connected as they are discrete in nature. The nervous system utilizes the neurons to transmit the signal. On the other hand, the circulatory system is used by the Endocrine System to transmit the signals. passage 3:What are the similarities between the nervous system and the endocrine system? Both the nervous system and endocrine system are devoted to maintaining homeostasis by coordinating and regulating the activities of other cells, tissues, organs, and systems. Both systems are regulated by negative feedback mechanisms. Chemical messengers are important in both systems, although their method of transmission and release differs in the two systems.

Human annotation

Sure! Based on the given passages, here are the key differences and similarities between the nervous system and the endocrine system: Differences: * The nervous system is made of neuron cells, while the endocrine system is made of glands. * Transmission in the nervous system occurs through electrochemical pulses, while in the endocrine system, it is done through chemicals called hormones. * The nervous system is continuous and interconnected, while the endocrine system consists of discrete organs. * The nervous system uses neurons to transmit signals, while the endocrine system uses the circulatory system. Similarities: * Both systems are devoted to maintaining homeostasis by coordinating and regulating the activities of other cells, tissues, organs, and systems. * Both systems are regulated by negative feedback mechanisms. * Chemical messengers are important in both systems, although their method of transmission and release differs. Therefore, based on the given passages, the nervous system and endocrine system have different structures and methods of transmission, but they share similar functions and regulatory mechanisms.

14775 / why should we serve others

Evidence

passage 1:Love your neighbour as yourself (Matthew 22:39). The Christian life is one of service to others, where we show love and kindness to everyone, even to those who do not treat us well. We can serve others in many ways, and we should ensure that we use every opportunity that we can.Relationships.he spirit of service should be seen in all aspects of our work. By providing a Second Mile Service, meaning that we go the extra mile for our customers and employers, we can serve others and help them in ways which they appreciate and find useful. If anyone forces you to go one mile, go with them two miles. passage 2:Question: Why should I want to serve God?. Answer: The fact that we should serve God is obvious in Scripture (see Luke 4:8). Why we should want to serve God is a more difficult question. Every Christian asked might have a different reason for serving God; different people are motivated by different things.However, the Bible does make clear that, when a person is in a real relationship with God, he will serve God.We should want to serve God because we know Him; an inherent part of knowing Him is a desire to serve Him. It’s always been God’s intention to make us like His Son, Jesus (Romans 8:29).f you want to want to serve God, the key is to get to know Him! Ask the Holy Spirit to reveal more of God to you (John 16:13). When we truly know God, who is love (1 John 4:8), our natural response is a desire to love and serve Him in return. passage 3:If we are serving others for those reasons, we are not serving or loving properly. Instead, we are serving others as a way to serve ourselves. This doesn’t mean we shouldn’t choose to serve if we feel it is the right thing to do in a given situation or to build and strengthen our character muscles.hen we learn to serve in this way our rewards are so much greater than if we were to serve with self-serving motives. Because we serve out of love with no stipulations or expectations of anything in return, it no longer matters what we get out of it.

Love your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:39) - We should serve others because it shows love and kindness to everyone, regardless of how they treat us. 2. The fact that we should serve God is obvious in Scripture (Luke 4:8) - We should serve God because He is worthy of our love and service, and it is a natural response to knowing Him. 3. If we are serving others for selfish reasons, we are not serving or loving properly (unable to answer based on given passages) - The passages do not provide explicit reasons why we should serve others without selfish motives. Therefore, the main reasons why we should serve others based on these passages are: * To show love and kindness to everyone, regardless of their treatment towards us. * To express our love and appreciation for God, who deserves our service and devotion.

Human annotation

Chard is a vegetable that has large, fleshy but tender deep green leaves and thick, crisp stalks. It is similar to spinach but has a stronger, more assertive flavor. Fresh young chard can be used raw in salads, while mature chard leaves and stalks are typically cooked or sautéed. Chard is in the same subspecies as beetroot and is cultivated for leaf production. It can be harvested while the leaves are young and tender or after maturity when the stems are slightly tougher. Chard is perishable and should be stored in the refrigerator for a minimum amount of time.

15461 / what is the difference between refined and unrefined coconut oil

Evidence

passage 1:• Refined coconut oil is made from the dried coconut fruit while unrefined coconut oil, also called pure or virgin coconut oil is made from the flesh of the fresh coconuts. • Unrefined coconut oil has a distinct aroma and flavor that is lost during refining. passage 2:However, refined coconut oil has a smoking point of 450 degrees F, whereas the smoking point of unrefined coconut oil is 350 degrees F. Because of its greater heat tolerance, refined coconut oil can be a better option for high-temperature cooking methods such as frying. passage 3:One of the distinguishing differences between refined and unrefined coconut oil is the taste. Because refined coconut oil is deodorized, it loses its signature coconut flavor and has no discernible taste or smell. However, unrefined oil carries a mild coconut flavor and aroma.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, the main differences between refined and unrefined coconut oil are: * Source: Refined coconut oil is made from dried coconut fruit, while unrefined coconut oil is made from the flesh of fresh coconuts. * Flavor and aroma: Unrefined coconut oil has a distinct coconut flavor and aroma, while refined coconut oil has a neutral taste and odor due to deodorization. * Smoking point: Refined coconut oil has a higher smoking point (450°F) than unrefined coconut oil (350°F), making it more suitable for high-temperature cooking methods like frying. Therefore, the choice between refined and unrefined coconut oil depends on personal preferences regarding flavor, aroma, and cooking methods.

Based on the given passages, here's how to poach an egg using a PoachPod®: 1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. 2. Crack an egg into the silicone poaching pod, being careful not to break the yolk. 3. Gently slide the pod into the boiling water, making sure it stays upright and no water gets in. 4. Cover the pot with a lid and let the egg cook for 6 minutes. 5. Use a large slotted spoon or tongs to lift the pod out of the hot water. 6. Flip the pod upside down over a plate and press the bottom to release the poached egg. So, to summarize, the steps to poach an egg using a PoachPod® are: 1. Bring water to a boil. 2. Crack egg into pod. 3. Float pod in boiling water. 4. Cook for 6 minutes. 5. Remove pod from water. 6. Release egg onto plate.

13432 / how to fix lift valve in toilet

Evidence

passage 1:The new flapper valve and chain for a 1.6 gallon per flush toilet. Step 1: Shutoff the water supply valve to the toilet. Step 2: Remove the old flapper valve by slipping it off the mounting arms. Remove what’s left of the broken lift chain from the lift arm. passage 2:Step 4: Open the water valve to fill the tank. Flush the toilet to check for correct operation. If needed, readjust the lift chain by moving the metal clip up or down a couple of links. When you’re satisfied, cut off the excess lift chain to prevent it from getting tangled. passage 3:Push the small solid end of the toilet lift arm into the flush handle. If a screw is included with your part, screw it in tightly. Push it until there is no more give and it is secure. The other end will hang freely in the air. Connect the chain to the third hole on the lift arm. This is the hole closest to the edge of the lift arm. Use the pliers to make sure it is securely fastened. Turn the water valve back on and test out the flush of the toilet. If the toilet flushes slowly, adjust the chain to make it a little tighter on the lift arm.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, here are the steps to fix a lift valve in a toilet: 1. Shut off the water supply valve to the toilet. 2. Remove the old flapper valve and any remaining pieces of the broken lift chain from the lift arm. 3. Install the new flapper valve and connect the chain to the third hole on the lift arm, making sure it is securely fastened. 4. Open the water valve to fill the tank and flush the toilet to test for correct operation. 5. Adjust the chain as needed to ensure a proper flush. Cut off any excess chain to prevent tangling. Note: If the toilet flushes slowly, adjust the chain to make it a little tighter on the lift arm.

Evidence

passage 1:DMSO is dimethyl sulfoxide, a by-product in converting trees to paper. It has industrial uses as an antifreeze and as a solvent for a wide range of chemicals. There are also a wide range of medical uses. It has a remarkable capacity to penetrate skin and tissue and enter the bloodstream. passage 2:DMSO relieves pain, reduces swelling, inflammation and much more. See 30 DMSO uses, from burns to scleroderma, plus directions, side effects, safety. DMSO pain relief is most frequently for muscles and joints. Applied to the skin, DMSO is an excellent anti-inflammatory and has many uses as a general pain reliever. It has been used with varying degrees of success in a great variety of medical ailments. Possible applications include: passage 3:DMSO as long been used to promote healing. People who have it on hand often use it for minor cuts and burns and report that recovery is speedy. 15905 / what is a transistor how does it work

Evidence

passage 1:The design of a transistor allows it to function as an amplifier or a switch. This is accomplished by using a small amount of electricity to control a gate on a much larger supply of electricity, much like turning a valve to control a supply of water.he base pulls these electrons from the emitter because it has a more positive voltage than does the emitter. This movement of electrons creates a flow of electricity through the transistor. The current passes from the emitter to the collector through the base. passage 2:A transistor is a miniature electronic component that can do two different jobs. It can work either as an amplifier or a switch: 1 When it works as an amplifier, it takes in a tiny electric current at one end (an input current) and produces a much bigger electric current (an output current) at the other.2 Transistors can also work as switches.ormally, the holes in the base act like a barrier, preventing any significant current flow from the emitter to the collector while the transistor is in its off state. A transistor works when the electrons and the holes start moving across the two junctions between the n-type and p-type silicon. passage 3:A transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify and switch electronic signals and electrical power.It is composed of semiconductor material with at least three terminals for connection to an external circuit.ollector current is approximately β (common-emitter current gain) times the base current. It is typically greater than 100 for small-signal transistors but can be smaller in transistors designed for high-power applications. Unlike the field-effect transistor (see below), the BJT is a low–input-impedance device.

When a small voltage is applied to the base, it controls the flow of current between the collector and emitter, allowing the transistor to act as an amplifier or a switch. Additionally, refined coconut oil is deodorized and has no taste or smell, while unrefined oil retains its distinctive coconut flavor and aroma.

13130 / how to soften sugar

Evidence

passage 1:3-Place brown sugar in a plastic container with a small piece of plastic wrap or foil over the sugar. Put a damp paper towel or napkin on top of the plastic/foil. Cover tightly. Remove damp paper towel in a couple of days. passage 2:A. Granulated sugar will harden when exposed to any type of moisture. Here is an easy way to make hardened granulated sugar soft again -- Preheat oven to lowest temperature, 150-200 degrees. Remove sugar from the package and put in an ovenproof container that will hold the sugar. Place in the warm oven for approximately 15 minutes. Tap sugar with a spoon. If it starts to fall apart, turn oven off and leave sugar in the oven for an hour or two to completely dry out. Always store granulated sugar in an airtight container. Store confectioners sugar in a cool, dry location (not the refrigerator). When it gets moist, it develops lumps. passage 3:How to keep it soft. The most efficient way to keep brown sugar soft is to keep it sealed in an airtight container. The trick is to limit the amount of air exposure as much as possible. Pack the sugar into the smallest container possible so that there is hardly any air space between the sugar and the lid.

14398 / when you have a bowel movement do you lose weight

Evidence

passage 1:Weight Loss and Calories. Your caloric intake and expenditure, rather than your bowel movements, are tied to healthy weight loss. Throughout the day, you consume calories in the form of food and drinks, which your body uses for energy.At the same time, your body burns calories at various rates, depending on the activities you perform.hoto Credit AVAVA/iStock/Getty Images. Hopping on the bathroom scale to weigh yourself before and after you have a bowel movement might be tempting, but unless your scale is highly accurate, you won't likely notice a difference in your body weight. passage 2:Photo Credit AVAVA/iStock/Getty Images. Hopping on the bathroom scale to weigh yourself before and after you have a bowel movement might be tempting, but unless your scale is highly accurate, you won't likely notice a difference in your body weight.hoto Credit AVAVA/iStock/Getty Images. Hopping on the bathroom scale to weigh yourself before and after you have a bowel movement might be tempting, but unless your scale is highly accurate, you won't likely notice a difference in your body weight. passage 3:A decrease in body weight after having a bowel movement does not come from a loss of body fat in stools. Body fat loss comes from creating a calorie deficit, which forces your body to burn stored fat for energy. A small amount of certain forms of fat, such as cholesterol, is normal in your feces.he fat in stools does not come from a loss of body fat, but rather from dietary fat intake that is not properly absorbed. Malabsorption of dietary fats may be caused by digestive conditions, such as celiac disease and Crohn's disease, pancreatitis, liver disease or cystic fibrosis.

Therefore, hopping on the bathroom scale before and after a bowel movement will not accurately reflect any weight loss due to the bowel movement itself.

12182 / how to get plastic out of clothes dryer

Evidence

passage 1:Instructions. Run the dryer on a regular setting for 20 minutes to soften the plastic. Scrape the plastic off with a wooden or plastic spatula or paint scraper, taking care not to damage the dryer's interior. Apply 1 to 2 tsp. nail polish remover to a clean cloth, and rub the plastic to dissolve it.Rub the area with a damp cloth to rinse the nail polish remover. Mix 1 tsp. liquid laundry soap with 1 cup water. Dip a clean cloth in this solution, and rub the area again.Rinse well with a cloth dipped in clean water.ave. Jupiterimages/BananaStock/Getty Images. A plastic coated bib or zip top bag gone astray probably won't melt in a dryer unless you're using the high heat setting, but if it does, it won't cause serious damage. Today's dryers are painted with a synthetic enamel coating that holds up well to heat and wear. passage 2:1 Answer from this member: This plastic will be extremely difficult to remove. You can try heating the plastic with a hair dryer or heat gun. Once it is heated, you may be able to peel off the plastic. You may not be able to get all of the plastic off. If not, you need to replace the drum or the entire dryer.If you want to replace the drum, I recommend calling a service technician to complete this type of repair.nce it is heated, you may be able to peel off the plastic. You may not be able to get all of the plastic off. If not, you need to replace the drum or the entire dryer. Soak a cloth in an acetone-based nail polish remover and leave it on the element for 5 minutes. Use this cloth to scrub the remaining plastic off of the element then wipe the coils with a clean, damp cloth.Remove any remaining nail polish remover residue with a cloth that has been dipped in a solution of warm water and dish soap, then rinse the coils with water.se this cloth to scrub the remaining plastic off of the element then wipe the coils with a clean, damp cloth. Remove any remaining nail polish remover residue with a cloth that has been dipped in a solution of warm water and dish soap, then rinse the coils with water.

Human annotation

To get plastic out of clothes dryer, run the dryer on a regular setting for 20 minutes to soften the plastic. Scrape the plastic off with a wooden or plastic spatula or paint scraper, taking care not to damage the dryer's interior. Apply 1 to 2 tsp. nail polish remover to a clean cloth, and rub the plastic to dissolve it. Rub the area with a damp cloth to rinse the nail polish remover. Then, mix 1 tsp. liquid laundry soap with 1 cup water and dip a clean cloth in this solution, and rub the area again. Rinse well with a cloth dipped in clean water. If the plastic is extremely difficult to remove, you can try heating it with a hair dryer or heat gun. Once heated, you may be able to peel off the plastic. However, you may not be able to get all of the plastic off, and you may need to replace the drum or the entire dryer.

A transistor is a semiconductor device that can function as an amplifier or a switch. It works by using a small amount of electricity to control a gate on a larger supply of electricity. The color of urine can have various meanings depending on the shade and context. Generally, a pale yellow color is considered normal, while a darker yellow or amber color can indicate dehydration. Red or pinkish urine can be a sign of blood in the urine, which may be caused by an infection, cancer, or other underlying conditions. Deep purple urine is associated with porphyria, a rare genetic disorder. Certain foods such as beets, berries, and fava beans can also temporarily change urine color. However, any persistent or significant changes in urine color should be evaluated by a healthcare professional to rule out potential health issues.

Human annotation

To poach an egg using a PoachPod, follow these steps: 1. Begin by bringing a large pot of water to a boil. 2. Gently slide an egg into your silicone poaching pod, taking care not to break the egg's yolk. 3. Float the poaching pod in the boiling water, ensuring that the pod stays upright and no water gets inside. 4. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and allow the egg to cook for 6 minutes. 5. After 6 minutes, remove the lid from the pot and use a large slotted spoon or tongs to carefully lift the poaching pod out of the hot water. 6. Flip the poaching pod upside down over a plate and gently press on the bottom to release the poached egg onto the plate.

12764 / what is the treatment when asset is discarded as per income tax act

Evidence

passage 1:For the purposes of Income Tax Act, a previous year is a distinct unit. In case an asset is discarded by the business but not sold, section 43(6) permits the scrap value of the asset to be reduced from the block in the previous year in which such asset is discarded.nder the block concept, all the assets falling within the same class and subject to same rate of depreciation are clubbed together and considered as single asset. Any alterations to the value of the block have to be strictly in accordance with the provisions of Chapter IV D of Income Tax Act, 1961. passage 2:Illustration 4 Note: The purpose of this illustration is to assist in clarifying the meaning of the explanation toparagraph 13 of theStandard. Facts: 1. The income before depreciation and tax of an enterprise for 15 years is Rs. 1000 lakhs per year, both as per the booksof account and for income-tax purposes.2. The enterprise is subject to 100 percent tax-holiday for the first 10 years under section 80-IA.llustration 4 Note: The purpose of this illustration is to assist in clarifying the meaning of the explanation toparagraph 13 of theStandard. Facts: 1. The income before depreciation and tax of an enterprise for 15 years is Rs. 1000 lakhs per year, both as per the booksof account and for income-tax purposes. passage 3:Pavan Jain S. Depreciation – a non cash expenditure allowed under Income Tax Act, 1961 following block concept. Under the block concept, all the assets falling within the same class and subject to same rate of depreciation are clubbed together and considered as single asset.he assessee is entitled to claim depreciation on the residual value of such discarded asset [ie., Opening WDV of such asset less scrap value] even though such discarded asset is not used for the purposes of business or profession in such year and subsequent years.

Human annotation

Based on the given passages, it is clear that when an asset is discarded by a business but not sold, the Income Tax Act allows the scrap value of the asset to be deducted from the opening work-in-progress (WDV) of such asset in the previous year in which it was discarded. This reduction is taken into account while computing the depreciation expense for the subsequent years. However, any changes made to the value of the block must be made strictly in accordance with the provisions of Chapter IV D of Income Tax Act 1961.

However, any changes made to the value of the block must be made strictly in accordance with the provisions of Chapter IV D of Income Tax Act 1961.
